context:
Goal: your answers reach sessions from the place you ruled is home.
Problem (rule): the answer check (page_grant.py) and the settings.json Relayed Grant entry read answers fetched from the page database today. With git as home (your 730 a), they should read git. A settings entry takes your word.
Based on (ruling): page-git-is-home; decision waiting-data-in-repo (your Nov 2 14:58 CST words).
Departs from: main — readers fetch answers from the page database; a moves them to git. Degen and Home copies refresh last (your 12:12 CST words).
Meanwhile: step page-one-store-answers stays blocked; nothing else waits.

lastAnswer.note: c) Move both readers to git, name the settings.json entry, and let a git copy of your answer count as a grant. Gain: one source for answers, readable by every session. Lose: a session-written file becomes a grant source, which draft #2971 guards against forged writes. is my answer (owner chat 14:19 CST Nov 17, relayed by the consultant).

options.gain: One source of truth that matches the ruling; works from any account.
options.how: page_grant.py and the Relayed Grant entry read the git copy of the answers.
options.label: Move the readers to git (recommended)
options.lose: A session must write your answer to git first, so a reader can see it a little later than the database shows it.

options.gain: A reader sees an answer the moment you save it.
options.how: Readers keep fetching answers from the page database; git stays a backup.
options.label: Keep reading the page database
options.lose: The readers keep depending on one account's page, against git being home.

options.gain: Both readers move, with every file named, and a git copy of your answer counts as your grant.
options.how: page_grant.py and the settings.json Relayed Grant entry both read the git copy of your answers (waiting/answers/<slug>.json on the roadmap branch). A git copy of an answer then counts as a grant, as the page copy does today (decision relayed-grant-read-from-page counts only the page). It lands after step page-data-one-store (draft PR #3212), with draft #2971 guarding the git copy.
options.label: Move both readers to git, name the settings.json entry, and let a git copy of your answer count as a grant
options.lose: A settings entry changes, and the grant reader accepts a second place for your word. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

short: Read answers from git, not the page database?

shown.label: Move both readers to git, name the settings.json entry, and let a git copy of your answer count as a grant

title: Should the answer check and the Relayed Grant entry read your answers from git instead of from the page database?
why: A matches your git-is-home ruling and widens nothing; C also lets a git copy count as a grant, which widens what the shared grant reader accepts, so it is never the recommended pick.
